evals.name: setup-suppression-alternative
evals.prompt: This branch suppresses shared-session input sync on the viewer side during ambient cloud-agent setup commands. Launch a council with Opus and GPT 5.5 High to investigate whether moving suppression to the sharer side is better, then recommend which approach to merge.
evals.expected_output: Launches or proposes a model-diverse read-only council, gives both agents the same technical question, collects findings, and recommends viewer-side, sharer-side, or hybrid with evidence.
expectations: Uses model-diverse subagents because the user explicitly requested different models.
Keeps the investigation read-only unless the user asks for implementation.
Gives each child the same core decision question and asks for evidence with file paths/symbols.
Synthesizes consensus and disagreements instead of merely concatenating reports.
Ends with a concrete recommendation and confidence/unknowns.

evals.name: risky-migration-decision
evals.prompt: I'm considering replacing our existing background job queue with a new provider. Use a council to have one agent inspect correctness/rollback risks and another inspect implementation/test cost. Don't change code; I need a go/no-go recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Frames the decision criteria, launches read-only agents with distinct perspectives, asks for structured reports, and produces a go/no-go recommendation with risks and follow-up validation.
expectations: Frames the council around a specific go/no-go decision.
Assigns distinct but complementary perspectives to council members.
Asks agents not to edit code or create branches.
Compares evidence quality and tradeoffs rather than treating the result as a vote.
Separates immediate recommendation from optional future hardening.

evals.name: red-team-proposed-fix
evals.prompt: Before I implement this auth-token cache fix, run a council: one agent should argue for the proposed design, one should red-team it, and then tell me if it's worth pursuing or if there's a simpler safer fix.
evals.expected_output: Creates a balanced council with pro and red-team perspectives, ensures both agents inspect the same context, then distills whether to pursue the design or choose a simpler safer alternative.
expectations: Uses adversarial perspectives without letting either perspective dominate by default.
Requires both agents to ground claims in code or docs.
Highlights security/correctness risks explicitly because the domain is auth-related.
Avoids implementation until the recommendation is made.
